## `agent`

tallow.agent — Agent task runtime Runtime support for @agent_task annotated functions. Provides sandboxing, resource tracking, and inter-agent communication.

### Types

- `AgentHandle` — Agent task handle
- `AgentStats` — Agent resource usage stats
- `Playbook` — SOAR playbook — compiled from YAML-like definition
- `PlaybookResult` — Result of executing a playbook
- `Alert` — Security alert for triage and escalation
- `IOCScanner` — Indicator of Compromise scanner
- `IOC` — Single indicator of compromise
- `IOCMatch` — Match result from IOC scanning
- `ContainmentResult` — Result of a containment action (all actions are simulated)
- `IncidentTimeline` — Incident timeline for event reconstruction
- `TimelineEvent` — Single event in a timeline
- `HuntResult` — Threat hunt result
- `HuntMatch` — Single match from a threat hunt query
- `CorrelationResult` — Correlated findings from multiple hunt results

### Functions

```tallow
fn status(self) -> AgentStatus
fn spawn(f: fn() -> T) -> AgentHandle<T>
fn spawn_agent(name: String, f: fn() -> T) -> AgentHandle<T>
fn await_all(handles: []AgentHandle<T>) -> []Result<T>
fn await_any(handles: []AgentHandle<T>) -> (usize, Result<T>)
fn parallel_map(items: []T, f: fn(T) -> R) -> []R
fn current_stats() -> AgentStats
```

- `status` — Get status
- `spawn` — Spawn an agent function (requires can_spawn permission)
- `spawn_agent` — Spawn a named agent
- `await_all` — Wait for all agents to complete
- `await_any` — Wait for first agent to complete
- `parallel_map` — Run functions in parallel, collect results
- `current_stats` — Get stats for current agent


- `await` — Wait with custom timeout (cannot exceed @agent_task timeout)

<a id="beehiiv"></a>
## `beehiiv`

beehiiv.tl — Type declarations for the tallow.beehiiv module Beehiiv publication API client. Interfaces with Beehiiv-powered Nuxt 3 sites to extract post metadata, content, and handle auth.

### Functions

```tallow
fn discover(url: str) -> Map
fn get_payload(url: str, build_id?: str) -> Map
fn get_post(url: str, build_id?: str) -> Map
fn set_jwt(jwt_token: str, base_url?: str) -> Bool
fn get_user(base_url?: str) -> Map
fn list_products(base_url?: str) -> Array
```

- `discover` — Discover a Beehiiv publication from a URL. Returns metadata map: base_url, build_id, post_slug
- `get_payload` — Fetch the Nuxt SSR _payload.json for a post URL. Returns raw payload as Map with post metadata and free_content_html.
- `get_post` — Extract post data from a Beehiiv URL. Combines _payload.json discovery with content extraction. Returns: title, subtitle, author, publish_date, free_content_html, free_content_text, has_paywall, audience, post_id, slug, url
- `set_jwt` — Inject a JWT token via /api/auth/set-token. The endpoint accepts any formatted JWT (no signature validation). Returns Bool success. Subscriber must exist in Beehiiv for premium access.
- `get_user` — Check current auth state via /api/auth/user. Returns user data Map if authenticated, or error.
- `list_products` — List available subscription products from /api/product. Returns Array of product Maps.


<a id="browser"></a>
## `browser`

tallow.browser — Browser automation via Chrome DevTools Protocol Browser operations require @legal annotation on the containing function. All operations return Result<T> and never panic. IMPORTANT: fetch() and browser.goto() are DISTINCT code paths: - fetch(url) makes a raw HTTP request and returns Response (no JS rendering) - page.goto(url) launches a browser, renders JavaScript, and returns NavigationResult If you need JavaScript-rendered content, use Browser.launch() + page.goto(). If you only need HTTP responses (APIs, static HTML), use fetch().

### Types

- `Browser` — Browser process handle. Created via Browser.launch(). Manages a headless (or visible) Chrome/Chromium instance via CDP.
- `Page` — Page handle. Represents a browser tab with navigation and DOM access. This is the primary interface for interacting with web content.
- `CdpCookie` — A CDP cookie as returned by Page.get_cookies().
- `AuthenticatedResponse` — Response from an authenticated HTTP request.
- `WpNonce` — A WordPress nonce extracted from a page.
- `LoginResult` — Result of a WordPress login attempt.
- `NavigationResult` — Navigation result returned by page.goto() and page.navigate(). Contains metadata about the completed navigation.
- `AntibotResolveStep` — One engine step of an AntibotResolveReport — an honest capability flag: available = engine could run under the current configuration, ran = it executed, note = what actually happened (never a fake success token).
- `AntibotResolveReport` — Result of page.resolve_antibot(): the detect → solve → retry loop with per-engine capability flags and the final page classification.
- `Element` — Element handle. Represents a DOM element for interaction and extraction. Element handles are tied to the page that created them.
- `BrowserContext` — Isolated browser context with per-proxy identity.
- `Crawler` — Web crawler with sitemap and link-following strategies.
- `PageCache` — Content-addressed page cache with BLAKE3 hashing.
- `ContentFingerprint` — Content fingerprint for deduplication and similarity detection.
- `StructuredData` — Extracted structured data from a web page.
- `PaginationInfo` — Pagination info detected from a page.
- `Dialog` — Dialog handling for alert, confirm, and prompt browser dialogs.
- `DialogHandler`
- `DialogResult`
- `Keyboard` — Page-level keyboard input control.
- `KeyboardEvent`
- `Mouse` — Page-level mouse input control.
- `MouseEvent`
- `PageContentResult`
- `ScriptTag`
- `StyleTag`
- `WaitResult`
- `ExposedFunction`
- `ExposedBinding`
- `PageEvent`
- `EventListener`
- `MediaEmulation`
- `VisionEmulation`
- `NetworkThrottle`
- `CpuThrottle`
- `HtmlParser` — Fast HTML parser for extracting data from raw HTML WITHOUT a browser. ~100x faster than browser-based extraction for static pages. For JavaScript-rendered content, use Browser.launch() + page.goto().
- `HtmlMeta` — Meta information extracted from HTML <head>.
- `PerfConfig` — Performance configuration presets for browser automation. Controls resource blocking, wait strategies, and stealth levels.
- `BrowserDaemon` — Persistent browser daemon for reusing browser instances across runs. Reduces cold-start latency by keeping Chrome processes warm.
- `BrowserDaemonStatus` — Status of the browser daemon process.
- `BrowserDaemonConfig` — Configuration for the browser daemon.
- `Screenshot` — Screenshot capture and comparison.
- `ScreenshotComparison`

- `AccessibilityReport` — Accessibility auditing tools (WCAG compliance).

- `AuditEntry` — Single audit log entry with chain hash.
- `AuditVerification` — Result of verifying the audit chain integrity.
- `AuditExport` — Exported audit log (JSON or text format).

- `ContentDedup` — BLAKE3-based content deduplication registry. Tracks content hashes to detect and count duplicate content.
- `DedupResult` — Result of checking content for duplication.

- `MemoryScrub` — Memory scrubbing after sensitive page visits. Ensures no residual data remains in browser state after processing sensitive content.

- `PiiClassifier` — PII tier classification following GDPR Art.9 categories. Classifies text into 5 tiers: T1 (Special category Art.9): health, religion, political, biometric, sexual orientation, ethnicity T2 (Sensitive PII): SSN, passport, financial accounts, tax IDs T3 (Standard PII): email, phone, name, physical address T4 (Pseudonymous): UUID, hex hashes, device IDs T5 (Non-PII): everything else

- `page_is_wordfence_challenge` — Check if the current page is a Wordfence JS challenge page ("One moment, please...").
- `page_bypass_wordfence` — Bypass the Wordfence JS challenge on the current page. Executes the challenge JS and waits for auto-redirect. Returns the final URL after bypass.
- `page_navigate_bypass_wordfence` — Navigate to a URL automatically bypassing Wordfence if encountered. Combines page.goto() + wordfence detection + auto-bypass.
- `page_wp_extract_rest_nonce` — Extract the WordPress REST API nonce (wp_rest) from the current page. Returns nil if not found (not logged in, or not an admin page).
- `page_wp_is_logged_in` — Check if the browser is currently logged into WordPress. Detects admin bar, logged-in body class, or logout links.
- `page_wp_login` — Attempt WordPress login via wp-login.php form. Navigates to login page, fills form, submits, detects outcome. Returns LoginResult with status: "success", "2fa_required", "failed", or "unknown".
- `page_wp_extract_all_nonces` — Extract ALL WordPress nonces from the current page. Returns array of WpNonce structs (REST, admin, etc.).
- `browser_context_create` — Create an isolated browser context.
- `crawler_from_sitemap` — Create a crawler from a sitemap.
- `crawler_from_links` — Create a crawler that follows links from a seed URL.
- `page_cache_create` — Create a page cache.
- `content_fingerprint_from_text` — Create a fingerprint from text content.
- `content_fingerprint_similarity` — Compare two fingerprints for similarity (0.0 to 1.0).
- `structured_data_extract` — Extract structured data (JSON-LD, OpenGraph) from HTML.
- `page_extract_all_text` — Extract all matching elements' text in ONE CDP call (batch mode).
- `page_extract_all_attrs` — Extract all matching elements with attributes in ONE CDP call.
- `page_block_non_essential` — Block non-essential resources for maximum speed.
- `page_wait_for_stable` — Wait until DOM is stable (no mutations for quiesce_ms).
- `page_detect_pagination` — Detect pagination pattern on the current page.
- `page_handle_cookie_consent` — Handle cookie consent banners automatically.
- `page_structured_data` — Extract structured data from current page.
- `page_capture_dom_snapshot` — Capture DOM snapshot (compact format for full-page extraction).
- `page_text_redacted` — Get page text with PII automatically redacted.
- `page_set_content` — Set the page HTML content directly.
- `page_content` — Get the full HTML content of the page.
- `page_add_init_script` — Add a script to run before page load.
- `page_add_script_tag` — Inject a script tag into the page.
- `page_add_style_tag` — Inject a style tag into the page.
- `page_wait_for_function` — Wait for a JS function/expression to return truthy.
- `page_wait_for_url` — Wait for navigation to a URL matching pattern.
- `page_wait_for_request` — Wait for an outgoing request matching URL pattern.
- `page_wait_for_response` — Wait for a response matching URL pattern.
- `page_wait_for_event` — Wait for a named event.
- `page_wait_for_timeout` — Wait for specified milliseconds (explicit sleep).
- `page_expose_function` — Expose a Tallow function to the page's JavaScript context.
- `page_expose_binding` — Expose a binding to the page (receives caller info).
- `page_on_console` — Listen for console messages from the page.
- `page_on_error` — Listen for uncaught page errors.
- `page_on_request` — Listen for outgoing network requests.
- `page_on_response` — Listen for network responses.
- `page_on_filechooser` — Listen for file chooser dialogs.
- `page_on_download` — Listen for download events.
- `page_emulate_media` — Emulate CSS media type and preferences.
- `page_emulate_vision` — Emulate vision deficiency (color blindness, blur). Valid: none, blurred, protanopia, deuteranopia, tritanopia, achromatopsia
- `page_throttle_network` — Throttle network to simulate connection conditions. Presets: offline, slow_2g, 2g, 3g, 4g, wifi, none
- `page_throttle_cpu` — Throttle CPU execution speed.
- `browser_surface_manifest` — Machine-readable manifest of the browser automation surface. Non-live: reports contract status for Browser.launch, Page.goto, cdp.pipe, etc.
- `browser_pipe_transport_status` — Status of the CDP pipe transport (--remote-debugging-pipe). Reports fail-closed: pipe transport is not yet implemented.
- `browser_fallback_boundary` — Boundary of the Phase 4 local/non-live browser fallback service.
- `browser_fallback_service_status` — Status of the Phase 4 browser fallback service (local, non-live planner).

- `capture_console` — Opt this page into console/error capture.  `drain_events("console", …)` and `on_console` need it; network events do not. It sends Runtime.enable, which anti-bot systems can detect, so it is not automatic. `on_console`, `on_error`, `expose_function` and `expose_binding` call it themselves.
- `close` — Close this tab. Pending `on_*` events are delivered before the close.
- `goto` — Navigate to a URL and wait for page load. This is the correct way to access JS-rendered pages. For HTTP-only requests (no JS), use fetch() instead.
- `navigate` — Navigate to a URL (alias for goto).
- `goto_antibot` — Anti-bot-aware navigation. Routes through the AntiBotOrchestrator so proxy selection/rotation, rate limiting, cookie farming, and CAPTCHA handling actually drive egress (relaunching the browser on the chosen proxy) instead of the raw `page.navigate` used by `goto`.  Optional second argument — a per-call egress/stealth map: {proxy: String, tor: Bool, stealth: Bool, tier: String} - proxy:    explicit proxy URL for THIS navigation ("socks5://…", "http://…"). Wins over the orchestrator's own selection. - tor:      true routes this navigation through Tor instances (implies per-domain circuit isolation). - stealth:  stealth on the relaunched browser (default true). - tier:     "tor" | "direct" | "datacenter" | "residential" | "isp" | "mobile". Classifies `proxy`, or "direct" pins this navigation to direct egress (no Tor fallback attempts). With no map, historical behavior applies (default Tor fallback pool + NOT wired on either plane: there is no interp arm and no native lowering. The orchestrator itself exists in Rust (src/browser/antibot.rs, invoked from src/stdlib/browser.rs) — what is missing is the per-plane dispatch. See docs/browser-native-gaps.md.
- `title` — Get the current page title.
- `url` — Get the current page URL.
- `content` — Full HTML of the current document, serialized from the live DOM (post-JS), not the bytes the server sent.
- `set_content` — Replace the document with `html`. The current DOM is discarded; the page handle stays bound, so later navigation still works.
- `wait_for_timeout` — Sleep for `ms`. Explicit wait; `elapsed_ms` reports what actually elapsed rather than echoing the request.
- `wait_for_function` — Poll a JS expression until it is truthy or `timeout_ms` elapses (default 30000). A timeout is `result: false`, not an error.
- `wait_for_url` — Wait until `location.href` matches `pattern` (`*` wildcards).
- `wait_for_event` — Wait for a CDP event — full method (`Page.loadEventFired`) or bare name (`loadEventFired`). Subscribe before the triggering action: events are not replayed.
- `wait_for_request` — Wait for an outgoing request whose URL matches `pattern`.
- `wait_for_response` — Wait for a response whose URL matches `pattern`.
- `add_init_script` — Run `script` before every document in this page loads.
- `add_script_tag` — Append a <script> to the current document. A value with a scheme is treated as a URL, anything else as inline source.
- `add_style_tag` — Append a <style> to the current document; same URL/contents rule.
- `emulate_media` — Emulate media type, colour scheme and reduced-motion preference.
- `emulate_vision` — Emulate a vision deficiency (none, blurredVision, deuteranopia, …).
- `throttle_network` — Apply a network preset: slow-3g, fast-3g, 4g or none. An unknown preset is an error, never a silent no-op.
- `on_console` — Register a `.tl` handler for page events. Delivery is deferred: the handler runs at the start of the next Page method call, with a `PageEvent` argument.
- `on_error` — Uncaught page errors (window.onerror / unhandled rejections).
- `on_request` — Outgoing network requests.
- `on_response` — Network responses.
- `on_filechooser` — File chooser dialogs.
- `on_download` — Download events.
- `expose_function` — Expose a JS function `name` that calls the `.tl` handler with the binding payload. Calls are buffered and delivered on the next Page call.
- `expose_binding` — Like `expose_function`, for bindings that also receive caller context.
- `drain_events` — Drain buffered page events, oldest first. `kind` empty means every category; `limit` 0 means all currently buffered. Taking removes them.
- `throttle_cpu` — Slow the CPU by `rate` (1.0 native, 4.0 = 4x slower).
- `query_selector` — Find the first element matching a CSS selector. Returns Err if no element matches.
- `query_selector_all` — Find all elements matching a CSS selector. Returns empty array if no elements match.
- `wait_for_selector` — Wait for an element matching the selector to appear in the DOM. Returns Err on timeout.
- `fill` — Fill a form field by CSS selector: focus, clear, then type the value character-by-character (real CDP Input.dispatchKeyEvent). clear_first defaults to true; delay_ms paces the keystrokes.
- `click` — Click the element matching a CSS selector (auto-waits actionability, scrolls into view, dispatches Input.dispatchMouseEvent).
- `select` — Select an <option> inside the <select> matching a CSS selector. by: "value" (default) | "label" | "index"; option is the match target.
- `resolve_antibot` — Detect → solve → retry orchestration over the page's CURRENT egress (ROADMAP #9). Sequences captcha.detect, the external-solver solve leg (incl. Turnstile), warmup/escalation capability flags, and a bounded re-navigation, returning an AntibotResolveReport whose per-engine steps carry honest {engine, available, ran, note} capability flags. Optional opts map: {solver_key: String, solver_service: String}.
- `reload` — Reload the current page.
- `go_back` — Navigate back in history.
- `go_forward` — Navigate forward in history.
- `scroll_by` — Scroll by pixel amounts.
- `scroll_to_bottom` — Scroll to the bottom of the page.
- `get_cookies` — Extract all browser cookies via CDP Network.getCookies. Returns an array of CdpCookie structs.
- `cookie_string` — Generate a Cookie header string for the given URL from the browser's cookie jar. Filters cookies by domain match, returns "name=value; name2=value2".
- `set_cookies_from_header` — Set cookies in the browser from a Cookie header string. domain: the domain to set cookies for (e.g. "ghraonline.com") path: the cookie path (default "/")
- `authenticated_get` — Make an authenticated HTTP GET request using browser cookies. Extracts cookies from the browser and sends via ureq through the runtime egress contract (proxy-aware; Tor by default) with a Cookie header. Returns {status: Int, body: String}.
- `authenticated_request` — Make an authenticated HTTP request with browser cookies. method: "GET", "POST", etc. body: request body string. Returns {status: Int, body: String}.

### `BrowserPool` methods

```tallow
fn create(max_size: i64 = 4, max_tasks: i64 = 100, headless: bool = true, egress: Map?) -> BrowserPool
fn acquire(pool: BrowserPool) -> AcquireResult
fn release(pool: BrowserPool, handle: BrowserHandle) -> BrowserPool
fn stats(pool: BrowserPool) -> PoolStats
fn health_check(pool: BrowserPool) -> HealthCheckResult
```

- `create` — Create a browser pool with max_size instances.  Optional trailing args: `headless` (default true) and an egress/stealth map `{proxy, tor, stealth, tier}`: - proxy:   proxy URL for the pool's browsers ("socks5://…", "http://…"). Wins over the TALLOW_PROXY env var. - tor:     true routes pool browsers through Tor instances (3), like TALLOW_TOR=1. - stealth: stealth flags on each pool browser launch. - tier:    "tor" | "direct" | "datacenter" | "residential" | "isp" | "mobile". Classifies `proxy` explicitly; "direct" is an explicit choice of direct egress (no env inheritance, no leak warning). Keys omitted from the map fall back to TALLOW_PROXY / TALLOW_TOR. Without any egress the pool launches DIRECT and warns (real-IP leak risk). Real arm: interp.rs BrowserPool.create; per-instance egress is resolved in pool.rs resolve_proxy and applied to BrowserConfig.proxy (Chrome's --proxy-server flag).
- `acquire` — Acquire a browser instance from the pool.
- `release` — Release a browser instance back to the pool.
- `stats` — Get current pool statistics.
- `health_check` — Run a health check on all pool instances.

<a id="crypto"></a>
## `crypto`

tallow.crypto — Cryptographic primitives All crypto is method-based, not library-based. Default: ML-KEM-768 (PQC), Argon2id (passwords), BLAKE3 (hashing) GUARD (E-1-02, 2026-09-13) This file is a declaration/dispatch surface only: no code path in the tree loads or executes these bodies (stdlib imports resolve via the interpreter / src/stdlib/crypto.rs dispatch tables). Every body below is therefore a deliberate fail-loud stub — `panic(...)` — so that if a future path ever executes one it aborts instead of silently returning mock data (a body here must never act as a security boundary). Verified: a forced-interpreter fixture aborts with `runtime error: panic: ...` (rc=1). Design: research/tallow-v1/cycle-02/07-crypto-design.md §D5; log: research/tallow-v1/exec/E-1-02-crypto-mechanicals.md. NOTE: `KeyPair.sign`/`KeyPair.verify` are NOT dispatched anywhere. A KEM key cannot sign; the interpreter silently falls back to its generic HMAC/hash methods for these names (src/interp.rs:13239/13371). Do not rely on them — the ML-DSA surface is `Cnsa2.sign`/`Cnsa2.verify` (dispatch: ml_dsa_87_*). FRONTEND NOTE (W2-09, 2026-09-13) `secret` is a *type-alias* qualifier only — `type X = secret T` (parser.rs:806-815, the sole qualifier site). `FieldDecl` has no qualifier slot (ast.rs:72-77), so `field: secret T` mis-parses: `secret` is read as the field type and `T` as the next field name → "expected ':', found ','". The two secret-Bytes fields below therefore go through the alias `SecretBytes`, which resolves to the same `Type::Secret(Bytes)` meaning (typeck.rs:323-336 alias qualifier; :701-705 named-alias resolution). Result: `tallow check stdlib/crypto.tl` rc=0 (was rc=1, errors 23:26/49:23). Log: research/tallow-v1/exec/W2-09-crypto-tl-shim.md.

<a id="csrf"></a>
## `csrf`

tallow.csrf — CSRF token auto-extraction and request signing CSRF tokens are security tokens embedded in web pages that must be included in subsequent requests. This module extracts them from a landing page and signs follow-up requests. Extraction sources (in priority order): - <meta name="csrf-token" content="..."> - <meta name="csrf-param" content="..."> - <input type="hidden" name="__RequestVerificationToken" value="..."> - <input type="hidden" name="authenticity_token" value="..."> - Cookie: XSRF-TOKEN - Cookie: csrf_token - Header: X-CSRF-Token

### Types

- `CsrfToken`
- `CsrfSession`
- `CsrfRequest`

### `CsrfSession` methods

```tallow
fn extract(url: String) -> CsrfSession
fn sign_request(session: CsrfSession, request: CsrfRequest) -> CsrfRequest
```

- `extract` — Extract CSRF tokens from a URL. Visits the page in browser mode and detects all known token patterns.
- `sign_request` — Sign a request with extracted CSRF tokens. Returns a new CsrfRequest with CSRF headers/fields injected.

<a id="cxense"></a>
## `cxense`

tallow.cxense — Cxense-metered paywall bypass. Cxense (Piano) meters news paywalls client-side: the full article IS in the served HTML but Cxense JS (cdn.cxense.com) gates it with a CSS overlay after a free-article quota. Bypass = reset meter cookies + whitelisted referrer + block Cxense JS + JSON-LD articleBody leak. See src/stdlib/cxense.rs for the implementation.

### Functions

```tallow
fn get_article(url: String, cookie_header: String?) -> Map

fn referrer_map() -> Map
```

- `get_article` — Extract a Cxense-metered article using every whitelisted referrer in order. Optional cookie_header (str) lets you pass harvested cookies (Cxense meter counters are stripped automatically).
- `get_with_referrer` — Fetch with one explicit referrer style: "drudge" | "social" | "google" | "facebook" | "hn"
- `extract_jsonld` — Pure JSON-LD `articleBody` extraction for a URL (no referrer tricks).
- `reset_meter` — Instructions for clearing the Cxense meter-cookie quota.
- `referrer_map` — The whitelisted referrer styles available to get_with_referrer.

<a id="entity"></a>
## `entity`

tallow.entity — general entity resolution / record linkage. Offline, deterministic clustering of records (stores, companies, operators, people) across independent sources: "is the operator of store A the same as company B?" Blocking keys and per-field similarity reuse tallow.recordlink's normalization / Soundex / Jaro-Winkler / token-set primitives. Resolution is deliberately conservative (high precision; false negatives preferred over false merges) and every threshold is an explicit argument. Candidate records are structs/maps with identity fields; the default field names are id / name / address / phone / email / domain and can be overridden per call via the optional `keys` argument. Both spellings of every function are equivalent: the documented capital `Entity.*` namespace and the lowercase `entity.*` alias route to the same native implementation. Determinism: records are ordered by record id before clustering, so canonical members, cluster ids (cl-0001, cl-0002, ...) and scores are stable across runs and input orders. Prefix ids with their source (e.g. "txabc:123", "sos:456") when merging across registries.

### Types

- `PairScore`
- `EntityMember`
- `EntityEvidence`
- `EntityCluster`

### `Entity` methods

```tallow
fn resolve(candidates: []Map, keys: Map?) -> []EntityCluster
fn pair(a: Map, b: Map, keys: Map?) -> PairScore
fn name_key(s: String) -> String
fn domain_key(s: String) -> String
fn address_key(s: String) -> String
fn phone_key(s: String) -> String
fn email_key(s: String) -> String
fn block_key(record: Map) -> String
fn name_similarity(a: String, b: String) -> Float
fn address_similarity(a: String, b: String) -> Float
fn phone_similarity(a: String, b: String) -> Float
fn email_similarity(a: String, b: String) -> Float
fn domain_similarity(a: String, b: String) -> Float
fn similarity(kind: String, a: String, b: String) -> Float
```

- `resolve` — Cluster candidate records into entities.
- `pair` — Pairwise verdict (match/no) + reason + per-field similarities.
- `name_key` — Canonical name key: sorted unique lowercase tokens (permutation-invariant).
- `domain_key` — Clean host ("WWW.Acme-shop-77.example:443/x" -> "acme-shop-77.example").
- `address_key` — Canonical street form ("123 Main St #4" -> "123 main street apt 4").
- `phone_key` — Digit-only phone ("(512) 555-0142" == "512-555-0142" == "+1 512 555 0142").
- `email_key` — Lowercased email (mailto: stripped, case-insensitive).
- `block_key` — Soundex(first name token) + ZIP5 compound key for a whole record (delegates to recordlink.block_key). Over-inclusive by design; pair scoring restores precision.
- `name_similarity` — Name similarity in [0,1]: max(Jaro-Winkler, token-set), normalized.
- `address_similarity` — Address similarity in [0,1] over canonical street forms.
- `phone_similarity` — Phone similarity in [0,1] over digit keys (blank-vs-blank = 0.5 neutral).
- `email_similarity` — Email similarity in [0,1] (equality is the strong signal).
- `domain_similarity` — Domain similarity in [0,1] (subdomain relation scores 0.9).
- `similarity` — Dispatch by field kind: name | address | phone | email | domain. Unknown kinds are a hard error, never a fabricated score.

### `entity` methods

```tallow
fn resolve(candidates: []Map, keys: Map?) -> []EntityCluster
fn pair(a: Map, b: Map, keys: Map?) -> PairScore
fn name_key(s: String) -> String
fn domain_key(s: String) -> String
fn address_key(s: String) -> String
fn phone_key(s: String) -> String
fn email_key(s: String) -> String
fn block_key(record: Map) -> String
fn name_similarity(a: String, b: String) -> Float
fn address_similarity(a: String, b: String) -> Float
fn phone_similarity(a: String, b: String) -> Float
fn email_similarity(a: String, b: String) -> Float
fn domain_similarity(a: String, b: String) -> Float
fn similarity(kind: String, a: String, b: String) -> Float
```

- `resolve` — Lowercase alias of Entity.resolve.
- `pair` — Lowercase alias of Entity.pair.
- `name_key` — Lowercase alias.
- `domain_key` — Lowercase alias.
- `address_key` — Lowercase alias.

<a id="escalation"></a>
## `escalation`

tallow.escalation — progressive rendering escalation. Automatically escalates through rendering strategies when simpler approaches fail. Inspired by ScrapingBee auto-mode and Firecrawl engine waterfall. Escalation ladder (0-5): 0: raw_http — fastest/cheapest, plain HTTP GET 1: cookie_jar — HTTP + session cookies 2: proxy — HTTP + rotated IP 3: browser_cdp — CDP browser rendering 4: browser_stealth — CDP + fingerprint spoofing 5: browser_premium — CDP + stealth + premium residential proxy

### Types

- `EscalationResult`

### `Escalation` methods

```tallow
fn fetch(url: String, max_level: String?, start_level: String?, timeout_ms: Int?) -> EscalationResult
fn scrape(url: String, extractor: String, max_level: String?) -> EscalationResult
```

- `fetch` — Progressive fetch: start at start_level, escalate to max_level on failure. Returns content from the first level that succeeds.
- `scrape` — Fetch + extraction. Built-in extractors: "title", "links", "text", "status".

<a id="forensics"></a>
## `forensics`

tallow.forensics -- Digital Forensics & STIX 2.1 Types Provides digital forensics primitives, cryptographic chain of custody, simulated memory/disk/network forensics, file carving, STIX 2.1 Structured Threat Information eXpression, and MITRE ATT&CK technique mapping. EvidenceChain Cryptographic chain of custody using BLAKE3 hash linking. Each evidence entry is linked to the previous via hash chaining, providing tamper-evident audit trails for legal proceedings. Static methods: EvidenceChain.create(case_id: String) -> EvidenceChain Creates a new evidence chain with a genesis hash. EvidenceChain.add_evidence(chain: EvidenceChain, description: String, hash: String) -> EvidenceChain Adds evidence to the chain (immutable update). Links new entry to previous via BLAKE3(prev_hash + evidence_hash + description + timestamp). EvidenceChain.verify(chain: EvidenceChain) -> bool Verifies the entire hash chain integrity. Returns false if any entry has been tampered with. EvidenceChain.export(chain: EvidenceChain) -> String Exports the chain as a JSON string for court-ready documentation. Fields: case_id (String), entries ([]EvidenceEntry), hash_chain (String), created_at (String), entry_count (i128) EvidenceEntry A single entry in an EvidenceChain. Fields: index (i128), description (String), evidence_hash (String), chain_hash (String), prev_hash (String), timestamp (String) MemoryDump Simulated memory forensics analysis. Static methods: MemoryDump.parse(data: String) -> MemoryDump Parses memory dump data. Extracts readable strings (4+ chars), detects PE/ELF/HTTP/SSH/DNS headers, computes entropy score. Fields: strings ([]String), headers ([]String), entropy (f64), size (i128), timestamp (String) DiskImage Simulated disk forensics. Static methods: DiskImage.mount(path: String) -> DiskImage Mounts a disk image. Detects format from extension: .e01 (EnCase), .dd/.raw (Raw), .vmdk (VMware), .vhd/.vhdx (Hyper-V), .qcow2 (QEMU). Fields: path (String), format (String), timeline ([]TimelineEntry), file_count (i128), mounted_at (String) FileCarver Simulated file carving with magic byte detection. Static methods: FileCarver.scan(data: String) -> []CarvedFile Scans data for magic byte signatures. Detects 7+ formats: PNG, GIF, PDF, ZIP/DOCX, JPEG, PE/EXE, ELF, SQLite, HTML, XML, RAR, 7-Zip. Returns array of CarvedFile structs. CarvedFile A file recovered by FileCarver. Fields: offset (i128), file_type (String), extension (String), magic (String), confidence (String) NetworkCapture Simulated pcap/network capture analysis. Static methods: NetworkCapture.reconstruct(data: String) -> NetworkCapture Reconstructs network sessions from capture data. Detects protocols (TCP, UDP, HTTP, DNS, SSH, etc.), extracts connections, counts packets. Fields: protocols ([]String), connections ([]Connection), packets (i128), size (i128), timestamp (String) Connection A network connection extracted from capture data. Fields: src (String), dst (String), protocol (String) VolatileData Simulated volatile data collection (live forensics). Static methods: VolatileData.collect() -> VolatileData Collects simulated volatile system data: running processes, active network connections, collection timestamp. Fields: processes ([]ProcessInfo), network_connections ([]Connection), timestamp (String) ProcessInfo A running process from volatile data collection. Fields: pid (i128), name (String), user (String), memory_kb (i128) StixBundle STIX 2.1 Bundle for structured threat intelligence exchange. Supports 8+ SDO types: threat-actor, malware, indicator, attack-pattern, campaign, identity, vulnerability, tool. Static methods: StixBundle.create() -> StixBundle Creates an empty STIX 2.1 bundle with auto-generated ID. StixBundle.add_object(bundle: StixBundle, type: String, properties: Map) -> StixBundle Adds a STIX Domain Object to the bundle (immutable update). Validates type against STIX 2.1 SDO types. Auto-generates id, spec_version, created, modified fields. StixBundle.export(bundle: StixBundle) -> String Exports the bundle as STIX 2.1 compliant JSON. Fields: type (String), id (String), objects ([]StixObject), spec_version (String) StixObject A STIX Domain Object within a bundle. Fields: type (String), id (String), spec_version (String), created (String), modified (String), + user properties AttackTechnique MITRE ATT&CK technique lookup and mapping. Static methods: AttackTechnique.lookup(id: String) -> AttackTechnique Looks up a MITRE ATT&CK technique by ID (e.g., "T1059", "T1566.001"). Returns technique info including name, tactic, description, platform, data sources, and MITRE URL. Returns "Unknown Technique" for unrecognized IDs. Fields: id (String), name (String), tactic (String), description (String), platform (String), data_sources ([]String), mitre_url (String) Known techniques (subset): T1003 - OS Credential Dumping T1021 - Remote Services T1027 - Obfuscated Files or Information T1048 - Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol T1055 - Process Injection T1059 - Command and Scripting Interpreter T1059.001 - PowerShell T1071 - Application Layer Protocol T1071.001 - Web Protocols T1078 - Valid Accounts T1105 - Ingress Tool Transfer T1190 - Exploit Public-Facing Application T1486 - Data Encrypted for Impact T1566 - Phishing T1566.001 - Spearphishing Attachment

_No declarations in the `.tl` surface — this module's native surface is documented in the prose above._

```tallow
fn query_selector(self, selector: String) -> Element?
fn query_selector_all(self, selector: String) -> []Element

```

- `content` — Get the full HTML content of this frame.
- `query_selector` — Find the first element matching a CSS selector within this frame. Returns nil if no element matches or frame is cross-origin.

<a id="http"></a>
## `http`

tallow.http — HTTP client/server NOT a stub. This header used to read "This is a stub — will be implemented as a native module in the compiler runtime", which was false: `src/stdlib/http.rs` implements get/post/put/delete/batch/ listen/server, the compiled plane lowers `http.batch` through `tallow_http_batch` (src/codegen.rs), and `Client`/`Server` constructors are handled inline in the interpreter. A module header that calls working code a stub is a false claim, not a coming-soon note.

### Types

- `Response`
- `HttpError` — A per-URL failure, typed: `kind` is `http_4xx`, `http_5xx` or `transport`; `status` is present only for an HTTP status, and `retryable` says whether a retry could plausibly help.
- `BatchResponse` — One entry of an `http.batch` result. Exactly one of `response`/`error` is meaningful: a success carries the response, a 4xx/5xx carries both (so the body stays readable), a transport failure carries only the error.
- `Client`
- `Server`

### Functions

```tallow
fn batch(target_urls: []String, concurrency: i64, headers: Map<String, String>) -> []BatchResponse
```

- `batch` — Fetch many URLs in one call — one typed entry per URL. A 4xx/5xx is a *result* carrying its body plus an `HttpError`, never a failed whole batch; a transport failure carries `HttpError` with `kind: "transport"` and no response. http.batch(target_urls, concurrency, headers) -> []BatchResponse

### `Response` methods

```tallow

fn json(self) -> Result<String>
```

```tallow

```


### `Server` methods

```tallow

```

<a id="jobs"></a>
## `jobs`

tallow.jobs — in-language scheduling bridge to the real browser scheduler. Bridges the CLI-only scheduler (`tallow browser schedule add|list|pause| resume|remove|run` in src/main.rs) to .tl scripts. Jobs are stored in and read from the same ScheduleStore the CLI and daemon use (~/.tallow-schedules.json). Execution is subprocess-based for now (`tallow run <script>`, mirroring the CLI run path); stage-2 warm-interpreter execution is out of scope. Capitalized namespace: Jobs.submit(...) / Jobs.list(...) / ... Lowercase alias: jobs.submit(...) / jobs.list(...) / ... (both resolve to the same module; the interpreter normalizes the case) Store override: set the TALLOW_SCHEDULE_STORE env var to point a script at a different store file (unset → ~/.tallow-schedules.json, same as CLI). schedule_spec is one string, validated with the CLI's own parsers: cron:0 8 * * * cron expression (5 fields; @yearly @monthly @weekly @daily @hourly shorthands accepted) — raw string kept every:5m fixed interval (10s.. : s/m/h/d/w units) — stored as Interval seconds, the store's canonical form daily:09:30 once per day at HH:MM (UTC unless tz_offset_secs set) bare "0 8 * * *" bare specs are cron (CLI --cron semantics) Max parallelism (reuses the scheduler core's cap model, scheduler.rs): the store-wide cap defaults to the TALLOW_MAX_CONCURRENT env var (40 if unset), clamped 1..256. jobs.set_max_concurrent(n) persists an explicit cap into the store JSON so it survives restarts. jobs.run_now never spawns more subprocesses than the effective cap: at capacity, extra run requests are queued (state "pending") and start FIFO as slots free up. A per-job {max_parallel: n} submit option additionally caps concurrent instances of that one job. jobs.status(id) reports idle | pending | running | done with active/queued/completed counters. run_now is ASYNC: it returns "running" (spawned) or "queued" (waiting for a slot) and completion bookkeeping (last_status/run_count) happens on a worker thread when the subprocess exits. Keep the calling script alive — e.g. poll jobs.status until "done" — otherwise that bookkeeping is lost when the process exits. If a scheduled script calls jobs.run_now on its own job, each level forks a fresh `tallow run` subprocess: bound the depth with the per-job max_parallel option. Errors are honest: a failed call (duplicate name, unknown id, invalid schedule_spec, run_now/status on a missing job, run_now on a job whose script file is missing) aborts the script with a descriptive message; nothing is recorded for runs that never started.

### Types

- `ScheduledJob` — Summary of one scheduled job, as returned by jobs.list().
- `JobStatus` — Run-state of one job, as returned by jobs.status(id).

### Functions

```tallow
fn submit(name: String, script: String, schedule_spec: String, opts: Map?) -> String
fn list() -> [ScheduledJob]
fn pause(id: String) -> Bool
fn resume(id: String) -> Bool
fn remove(id: String) -> Bool
fn run_now(id: String) -> String
fn status(id: String) -> JobStatus
fn set_max_concurrent(n: Int) -> Bool
fn get_max_concurrent() -> Int
```

- `submit` — Submit a new job. The job id is its unique name (duplicates are rejected). Returns the job id.  Optional 4th arg (a Map): {max_parallel: n} caps how many instances of this job may run concurrently (clamped 1..256, persisted on the job). Extra map keys are ignored.
- `list` — List all jobs in the store as ScheduledJob structs.
- `pause` — Pause a job by id (it will not fire until resumed). Errors on unknown id.
- `resume` — Resume a paused job by id; recomputes next_run. Errors on unknown id.
- `remove` — Remove a job by id. Errors on unknown id.
- `run_now` — Run a job's script once right now, as a subprocess (`tallow run`), and record the outcome (last_status/last_run/run_count) when it finishes. Async: returns "running" when spawned, "queued" when the concurrency cap is full (the request is queued FIFO and starts as slots free up). Real errors (no fake success) when the job or its script file does not exist. Poll jobs.status(id) until "done" to observe completion.
- `status` — Run-state of one job: idle | pending | running | done plus counters. Errors on unknown id.
- `set_max_concurrent` — Persist the store-wide concurrency cap (clamped 1..256). Survives restarts via the ScheduleStore JSON. Initial default: TALLOW_MAX_CONCURRENT env var, else 40 (same as the scheduler daemon).
- `get_max_concurrent` — Effective store-wide concurrency cap (persisted value, else the TALLOW_MAX_CONCURRENT env var, else 40).

tallow.jwt — JSON Web Token analysis, forgery, and attack. Parse JWTs without verification, forge HMAC-signed tokens, and run standard JWT attacks: alg:none, weak secret brute force, kid injection, and alg confusion.

### Types

- `JWT`
- `JWTAttackResult`

```tallow

```

- `parse` — Decode a JWT without verification — returns header, payload, algorithm, and signature.
- `forge` — Create a signed JWT with HMAC (HS256, HS384, HS512).
- `attack_none` — Attack: replace algorithm with "none" and remove the signature.
- `attack_weak_secrets` — Attack: brute force HMAC secrets from a wordlist. Returns found secrets.

<a id="legal"></a>
## `legal`

tallow.legal — @legal runtime + audit record persistence Runtime half of the @legal system. Compile-time annotation checks run in the legal/consent/erasure AST passes; this module's functions persist audit, consent, and erasure records to the legal data directory (env TALLOW_LEGAL_DIR, default ~/.tallow/legal) as JSONL files: - log_audit → audit_log.jsonl - read_audit_log → reads audit_log.jsonl back - consent_register/consent_check → consent_register.jsonl - erasure_request / subject_access_request → erasure_requests.jsonl Report-generation / DORA / AI-Act / model-provenance functions are NOT implemented by this backend and return an honest error when called.

### Types

- `AuditEntry` — Audit log entry persisted by log_audit / read back by read_audit_log
- `ComplianceResult`
- `CraReport` — CRA compliance report
- `CraCheckItem`
- `AlgorithmPolicy` — Crypto algorithm policy entry
- `Nis2Report` — NIS2 Art.21 compliance report
- `Nis2Measure`
- `DoraCitIncident` — DORA ICT incident record per Art.19
- `AiSystemInfo` — AI system registration for EU database (Art.71)
- `InferenceEntry` — AI inference log entry (Art.12 record-keeping)
- `AiInferenceLog` — AI inference log with tamper-evident hash chain
- `HumanApproval` — Human approval gate result
- `ModelProvenance` — Model provenance chain (Annex IV technical documentation)

### Functions

```tallow
fn log_audit(entry: AuditEntry) -> Result<()>
fn read_audit_log(path: String) -> Result<[]AuditEntry>
fn consent_register(subject: String, purpose: String) -> String

fn subject_access_request(subject: String) -> String

fn dora_classify(incident: DoraCitIncident) -> DoraCitIncident

```

- `log_audit` — Write audit entry to the JSONL audit log (TALLOW_LEGAL_DIR/audit_log.jsonl)
- `read_audit_log` — Read audit log entries back from the JSONL audit log (default TALLOW_LEGAL_DIR/audit_log.jsonl when path is empty)
- `consent_register` — Record explicit consent (GDPR Art.6/7, CCPA) — appends to TALLOW_LEGAL_DIR/consent_register.jsonl and returns a record id
- `consent_check` — True iff the consent register holds a current registration for the subject + purpose pair
- `erasure_request` — Log a GDPR right-to-erasure request (Art.17) — appends to TALLOW_LEGAL_DIR/erasure_requests.jsonl and returns a request id
- `subject_access_request` — Log a GDPR subject-access request (Art.15) — same register as erasure requests, distinct event type; returns a request id
- `generate_report` — Generate compliance report
- `check_compliance` — Check compliance for jurisdiction
- `cra_audit` — Generate CRA compliance report for the current project
- `nis2_audit` — Generate NIS2 Art.21 compliance report
- `dora_incident_new` — Create a new ICT incident with auto-generated ID and timestamp
- `dora_classify` — Auto-classify incident severity per DORA RTS criteria CRITICAL: critical_function_impaired AND (duration > 24h OR records > 100K) HIGH:     critical_function_impaired OR clients > 10% OR records > 5,000 MEDIUM:   clients > 1% OR duration > 2h OR cross_border LOW:      all other incidents
- `dora_report` — Generate DORA-compliant incident report JSON for regulatory notification
- `ai_inference_log_create` — Create a new inference log for an AI system
- `ai_inference_log_entry` — Log an inference event (input hashed for privacy)
- `ai_inference_log_verify` — Verify log integrity (recompute hash chain)
- `ai_inference_log_export` — Export log as JSON for Art.12 audit
- `human_approval_request` — Request human approval for a high-risk decision (Art.14)
- `model_provenance_create` — Create a new model provenance record
- `model_provenance_set` — Set a provenance field (immutable update)
- `model_provenance_attest` — Attest provenance with BLAKE3 cryptographic hash
- `model_provenance_verify` — Verify attestation integrity
- `model_provenance_export` — Export provenance as JSON (for Annex IV documentation)

tallow.net — Networking primitives (IPPool, sockets, DNS, TLS, QUIC, WebSocket, PacketCapture) Phase 23: Stealth & Advanced Networking types

### Types

### Functions

```tallow
fn tor_pool_create(size: i32) -> TorPool
fn onion_addr(address: String) -> OnionAddr
fn proxy_chain_create(hops: []String) -> ProxyChain
fn tunnel_wireguard(endpoint: String, key: String) -> Tunnel
fn grpc_server_create(port: i32) -> GrpcServer
fn grpc_client_connect(endpoint: String) -> GrpcClient
fn traffic_shape_create(padding: i32, rate_ms: i32, cover_traffic: bool) -> TrafficShape
fn transport_obfs4(bridge: String) -> Transport
fn transport_meek(url: String) -> Transport
fn transport_snowflake(broker: String) -> Transport
```

- `tor_pool_create` — Create a Tor connection pool with the given number of circuits. Routes traffic through the local Tor SOCKS5 proxy (127.0.0.1:9050) and rotates circuits over its control port (127.0.0.1:9051). Optional extra args select a different daemon: tor_pool_create(size, "host:port"[, control]). ready/rotation reflect live daemon probes, never constants.
- `onion_addr` — Create a typed .onion hidden service address. Validates that the address ends with ".onion".
- `proxy_chain_create` — Create an ordered multi-hop proxy chain. Accepts array of proxy specs: "socks5://host:port", "http://host:port", "tor"
- `tunnel_wireguard` — Create a WireGuard tunnel to the given endpoint with the provided public key.
- `grpc_server_create` — Create a gRPC server bound to the given port.
- `grpc_client_connect` — Connect to a gRPC endpoint.
- `traffic_shape_create` — Create a TrafficShape for traffic analysis resistance. padding: target padding size in bytes (0 = no padding) rate_ms: constant-rate interval in milliseconds cover_traffic: whether to generate cover traffic when idle
- `transport_obfs4` — Create an obfs4 pluggable transport connection. obfs4 makes traffic look like random noise, defeating DPI-based censorship. bridge: address of the obfs4 bridge (e.g., "bridge.example.com:443")
- `transport_meek` — Create a meek (domain-fronting) transport connection. Meek tunnels traffic through CDN-hosted HTTPS, making it look like normal web browsing to a permitted domain. url: the fronting URL (e.g., "https://cdn.example.com")
- `transport_snowflake` — Create a snowflake (WebRTC) transport connection. Snowflake uses WebRTC peer connections through volunteer browser proxies, making traffic indistinguishable from video calls. broker: URL of the snowflake broker (default: Tor Project broker)

<a id="osint"></a>
## `osint`

tallow.osint -- OSINT Intelligence Types and Operations Provides intelligence seed types with provenance tracking, subdomain enumeration, technology fingerprinting, domain/IP/ASN intelligence, email intelligence (SPF/DMARC/breach), and privacy-safe document metadata extraction. Target Intelligence seed type. Creates typed targets with automatic provenance tracking for audit trails. Constructors: Target.domain("example.com") -> Target { kind: "domain", value, provenance } Target.ip("192.168.1.1") -> Target { kind: "ip", value, provenance } Target.email("user@ex.com") -> Target { kind: "email", value: Private, provenance } shop-78.example("Acme Corp") -> Target { kind: "org", value, provenance } Methods: target.enumerate_subdomains() -> []SubdomainResult Enumerates subdomains via CT logs (crt.sh) and DNS brute-force. Returns array of SubdomainResult structs with source provenance. SubdomainResult Result from subdomain enumeration. Fields: subdomain (String), source ("ct_logs" | "dns_brute"), provenance ([]Provenance) TechStack Technology fingerprinting via HTTP headers and HTML analysis. Static methods: TechStack.detect("https://example.com") -> TechStack Fetches URL, matches against ~50 technology signatures. Returns detected technologies with confidence levels. Result fields: url (String), technologies ([]Technology), provenance ([]Provenance) Technology Individual detected technology. Fields: name (String), category (String), version (String), confidence ("high"|"medium"|"low") DomainIntel Domain intelligence via WHOIS queries and DNS resolution. Static methods: DomainIntel.whois("example.com") -> DomainIntel Performs WHOIS lookup via TCP (port 43) with IANA referral. Parses: registrar, creation_date, expiration_date, updated_date, nameservers, status. Returns raw WHOIS text plus parsed fields. DomainIntel.dns_history("example.com") -> DomainIntel Resolves A/AAAA DNS records for the domain. Returns DnsRecord structs with type and value. Result fields: domain (String), raw (String), registrar (String), creation_date (String), expiration_date (String), updated_date (String), nameservers ([]String), status ([]String), provenance ([]Provenance) ASNIntel Autonomous System Number intelligence via WHOIS. Static methods: ASNIntel.lookup("8.8.8.8") -> ASNIntel Queries ARIN WHOIS for IP-to-ASN information. Parses: asn_number, org_name, country, network_range. Result fields: ip (String), raw (String), asn_number (String), org_name (String), country (String), network_range (String), provenance ([]Provenance) EmailIntel Email intelligence with SPF/DMARC analysis and breach checking. Static methods: EmailIntel.from("user@example.com") -> EmailIntel Creates email intel struct. Email is automatically wrapped in Value::Private for PII protection. Domain is extracted. Instance methods: .check_spf() -> SpfResult DNS TXT lookup for SPF record, parses mechanisms (ip4:, ip6:, include:, redirect=, all). Caps recursive includes at RFC 7208 limit. Uses Cloudflare DNS-over-HTTPS for TXT record resolution. .check_dmarc() -> DmarcResult DNS TXT lookup for _dmarc.domain, parses DMARC tags: v, p, rua, ruf, pct, adkim, aspf, sp, fo. .breach_check() -> BreachResult HIBP k-anonymity check: SHA1 prefix query to Have I Been Pwned. Returns COUNT ONLY -- never passwords or breach details. Privacy-safe: only first 5 hex chars of SHA1 sent to API. SpfResult Result from SPF record analysis. Fields: raw (String), mechanisms ([]String), all_qualifier ("+"|"-"|"~"|"?"), includes ([]String), provenance ([]Provenance) DmarcResult Result from DMARC record analysis. Fields: raw (String), version (String), policy (String), rua (String), ruf (String), pct (String), adkim (String), aspf (String), provenance ([]Provenance) BreachResult Result from breach check (count only, never passwords). Fields: count (Int), checked_at (String RFC3339), provenance ([]Provenance) DocumentMeta Document metadata extracted from files with privacy enforcement. Static methods: parse_document(bytes) -> DocumentMeta Detects format via magic bytes and extracts metadata. Supported formats: - PDF (%PDF): Title, Author (Private), Subject, Creator, Producer, dates - EXIF (JPEG/TIFF): Make, Model, DateTime, Artist (Private), GPS latitude/longitude (Private, decimal degrees) - OOXML (.docx/.xlsx/.pptx): Title, Creator (Private), Subject, Description, Created, Modified, LastModifiedBy (Private) - OLE2 (.doc/.xls/.ppt): Returns "unsupported format" error PII fields (author, artist, creator, GPS coordinates) are automatically wrapped in Value::Private for compile-time privacy enforcement. Result fields: format (String: "PDF"|"EXIF"|"OOXML"), plus format-specific metadata fields, provenance ([]Provenance) DnsRecord Individual DNS record from dns_history. Fields: type (String: "A"|"AAAA"), value (String: IP address) Provenance Audit trail entry tracking data origin and transformations. Fields: source (String), operation (String), timestamp (String RFC3339)

_No declarations in the `.tl` surface — this module's native surface is documented in the prose above._

<a id="provenance"></a>
## `provenance`

tallow.provenance — collection-level provenance & source grading. Every fetched/crawled fact gets a sticker: where it came from, how fresh it is, which egress path fetched it, the HTTP outcome, a content fingerprint, a validation chain, a folded numeric confidence, and a final letter grade. Built on the same freshness/validation model as the Tallow provenance tracker (src/browser/provenance.rs) — those types are aliased, not duplicated. Capitalized namespace: Provenance.record(...) / Provenance.grade(...) Lowercase alias: provenance.record(...) / provenance.grade(...) (both resolve to the same module; interpreter normalizes the case) Typical flow: let rec = Provenance.record( "https://example.com/prices", // source_url "us-res-01", // egress_label "residential", // egress_tier 200, // status_code Provenance.hash_body(body)) // body_hash (sha256 hex) rec = Provenance.add_validator(rec, "html_parse", true, 0.05, "parsed ok") rec = Provenance.grade(rec) // folds confidence, assigns A..F print(rec.grade) // "A" print(rec.confidence) let json = Provenance.to_json(rec) // durable roundtrip let copy = Provenance.from_json(json) rec = rec.grade() // method form works too

### Types

- `ValidationStep`
- `CollectionRecord`

### Functions

```tallow
fn record(source_url: String, egress_label: String, egress_tier: String, status_code: Int, body_hash: String) -> CollectionRecord
fn record_at(source_url: String, egress_label: String, egress_tier: String, status_code: Int, body_hash: String, fetched_at: Int) -> CollectionRecord
fn add_validator(rec: CollectionRecord, validator: String, passed: Bool, adjustment: Float, note: String?) -> CollectionRecord
fn grade(rec: CollectionRecord) -> CollectionRecord
fn freshness(rec: CollectionRecord) -> String
fn hash_body(body: String) -> String
fn to_json(rec: CollectionRecord) -> String
fn from_json(json: String) -> CollectionRecord
```

- `record` — Create a record. fetched_at defaults to now; base confidence defaults to 0.8. Optional trailing args: fetched_at (Int), base_confidence (Float).
- `record_at` — Create a record with an explicit fetch timestamp (unix epoch seconds).
- `add_validator` — Append a validation step (passed adds |adjustment|, failed subtracts it).
- `grade` — Recompute confidence over the validator chain and assign the letter grade. Rubric: 200 = A, other 2xx = B, 3xx = C, 4xx = D, 5xx/none = F; downgraded by egress tier (datacenter/proxy −1, tor −2), confidence (< 0.7 −1, < 0.5 −2) and freshness (Stale −1, Old −2).
- `freshness` — Freshness label of a record: "Fresh" | "Recent" | "Stale" | "Old" (cutoffs < 15 min, < 6 h, < 24 h — same bands as the browser model).
- `hash_body` — sha256 hex fingerprint of a fetched body (64 lowercase hex chars).
- `to_json` — Serialize a record (incl. validators) to durable JSON.
- `from_json` — Parse a record back from the JSON produced by to_json().

<a id="rate-limit"></a>
## `rate_limit`

tallow.rate_limit — token-bucket rate limiting, backoff, and request distribution. Token bucket rate limiter for pacing API calls, exponential backoff with jitter for retry logic, and URL batching for concurrent request distribution.

### Types

- `RateLimiter`
- `DistributionPlan`

### `RateLimiter` methods

```tallow
fn new(max_per_second: Float) -> RateLimiter
fn wait(self, timeout_ms: Int?) -> Bool
fn try_acquire(self) -> Bool
fn available(self) -> Float
fn backoff(attempt: Int) -> Int
fn distribute(urls: [String], concurrency: Int) -> DistributionPlan
```

- `new` — Create a rate limiter that allows max_per_second requests per second.
- `wait` — Block until a token is available, or timeout_ms expires. Returns true if acquired.
- `try_acquire` — Try to acquire a token without blocking. Returns true if acquired.
- `available` — Current number of available tokens (may be fractional).
- `backoff` — Exponential backoff with jitter. Returns delay in milliseconds for attempt N. attempt 1→1s, 2→2s, 3→4s, 4→8s, 5→16s, 6→32s, cap at 60s.
- `distribute` — Distribute URLs into batched groups for concurrent processing.


<a id="recordlink"></a>
## `recordlink`

tallow.recordlink — record linkage / entity resolution primitives. Offline scoring for deciding whether two records (names + optional US-format addresses) refer to the same real-world entity. All functions are pure and deterministic — no network access. Pair with tallow.geocode for address parsing and tallow.sourcegrade for provenance.

### Types

- `MatchResult`

### Functions

```tallow
fn normalize_name(s: String) -> String
fn name_key(s: String) -> String
fn jaro(a: String, b: String) -> Float
fn jaro_winkler(a: String, b: String) -> Float
fn token_set(a: String, b: String) -> Float
fn jaccard(a: String, b: String) -> Float
fn soundex(s: String) -> String
fn block_key(name: String, address: String) -> String
fn exact(a: String, b: String) -> Bool
fn name_similarity(a: String, b: String) -> Float
fn address_similarity(a: String, b: String) -> Float
fn score(name_a: String, addr_a: String, name_b: String, addr_b: String) -> MatchResult
```

- `normalize_name` — Canonical name: lowercase, punctuation stripped, whitespace collapsed.
- `name_key` — Sorted unique token set — permutation-invariant name key.
- `jaro` — Jaro similarity in [0,1].
- `jaro_winkler` — Jaro–Winkler similarity in [0,1] (prefix boost).
- `token_set` — Token-set similarity in [0,1] (reorder / partial-overlap tolerant).
- `jaccard` — Jaccard index over token sets in [0,1].
- `soundex` — 4-character Soundex code ("Miller" -> "M460").
- `block_key` — Coarse blocking key: Soundex(first name token) + ZIP5 of address.
- `exact` — Normalized exact-equality test for names.
- `name_similarity` — Best name similarity in [0,1]: max(Jaro–Winkler, token-set).
- `address_similarity` — Address similarity in [0,1] over canonical street forms.
- `score` — Full pairwise record score. Verdicts: match / probable / possible / weak / no.

<a id="relay-room"></a>
## `relay_room`

tallow.relay_room — Relay room sessions on the SendTallow product relay (WebSocket wire; raw postcard Message frames — same wire as the product's browser client). Stage 3 / Slice 2. Legacy 2-peer rooms (`join`): the relay pairs two peers on the same code phrase; `RoomJoined.peer_present` reports whether the other side is already waiting; PeerArrived / PeerDeparted arrive as events. Multi-peer rooms (`join_multi`): the relay assigns a peer id (`RoomJoinedMulti{peer_id, existing_peers}`); peers join/leave raise peer_joined / peer_left events; payloads travel in Targeted envelopes (broadcast = to_peer 255). Password auth: pass the relay's password to join/join_multi; wrong or missing password → hard error ("relay rejected join: authentication failed").

### Types

- `RelayRoom`
- `RelayEvent`
- `RelaySendOutcome`

### `RelayRoom` methods

```tallow
fn join(url: String, code: String, password: String = "") -> RelayRoom
fn join_multi(url: String, code: String, capacity: i64 = 0, password: String = "") -> RelayRoom
fn send(self, data: String) -> RelaySendOutcome
fn send_bytes(self, data: Bytes) -> RelaySendOutcome
fn send_to(self, peer_id: i64, data: String) -> RelaySendOutcome
fn recv(self, timeout_ms: i64 = 10000) -> RelayEvent
fn leave(self)
fn status(self) -> RelayRoom
fn room_id(code: String) -> String
```

- `join` — Join a legacy 2-peer room (ws://host:port/ws). Hard error on auth reject/timeout.
- `join_multi` — Join a multi-peer room; relay-assigned peer ids are 0-based (0 <= existing_peers < capacity).
- `send` — Send a payload (utf-8 string; legacy raw / multi broadcast).
- `send_bytes` — Send exact bytes (legacy raw / multi broadcast).
- `send_to` — Send a payload to one peer in a multi room (255 = broadcast).
- `recv` — Receive the next event or payload. kind: payload | peer_arrived | peer_departed | peer_joined | peer_left | timeout | closed | error
- `leave` — Close the room session.
- `status` — Live status of a room handle (same shape as join's result).
- `room_id` — Room id (hex) for a code phrase, via the same compatibility rule every client uses (`resolve_room_id`): the *shape* of the code selects the derivation, so an 8-symbol passcode is an Argon2id derivation and legacy phrases are BLAKE3. Refuses anything that is not the accepted 8-symbol mint rather than deriving a room no other peer would join.

<a id="sitescan"></a>
## `sitescan`

tallow.sitescan — comprehensive website + infrastructure scanning module. READ-ONLY · PUBLIC-DATA · GET-ONLY · FAIL-CLOSED EGRESS (TOR-FIRST). One call returns a depth-labelled picture of a target website and the infrastructure underneath it — no component silently dropped: D1 surface homepage fetch (redirect chain, ALL headers, security-header matrix, cookies, link-graph rollup, tech fingerprint, forms + inputs), robots.txt (parsed rules + sitemaps), sitemap.xml (url count / index children), third-party hosts D2 pages robotted same-site crawl to link_depth (default 3): per page url/final_url/status/content-type/bytes/title/depth, links in+out, assets, forms; separate documents rollup D3 assets inventory by kind + host: images/media/fonts/scripts/styles/ iframes; CSS fetched & mined (url(), @import → fonts/images); JS fetched & mined for endpoints — absolute URLs, fetch/axios/XHR call targets, api-shaped literal paths, websocket endpoints, sourceMappingURL refs — with per-finding source provenance; inline scripts mined too D4 infra DNS via DoH (A/AAAA/CNAME/MX/TXT/NS/SOA/CAA), subdomains via certificate transparency (crt.sh: cert rows, issuers, latest expiry + days remaining); optional DNS brute + Wayback CDX; rdap for the domain and resolved IPs (+ netblock rollup) D5 network TCP port sweep on resolved IPs — STRICTLY gated: every target must be inside an explicit owner-authorized CIDR (opts.authorized_cidr), re-checked per IP against the scope authorizer; out-of-scope targets are refused, never scanned Depth parameter: scan(target, depth, opts) 1 | "surface" · 2 | "pages" · 3 | "assets" · 4 | "infra" · 5 | "network" | "full" (Int is the typed contract; stage names also accepted at runtime) opts (JSON string, all optional): max_pages (default 25) · link_depth (3) · max_js (10) · max_css (5) · include_subdomains (false) · brute (false) · wayback (false) · only: ["surface"|"pages"|"assets"|"infra"|"network"] · ports: [..] (D5) · authorized_cidr ("x.x.x.x/nn" — required for any D5 result) · port_timeout_ms (1500) Aggregation: every stage carries counts + timing; the envelope carries module/version/target/host/apex/depth/stage_order/limits/errors/ok; report() renders the full Markdown findings document — the scope, depth & limits block and each stage's findings, plus a plainly-labelled errors & notes section (nothing silently dropped). Error contract (match on prefixes): sitescan:param: bad argument (type/value) sitescan:net: transport failure (only genuine transport errors) sitescan:http: non-2xx after retries (API stages) sitescan:shape: upstream body malformed sitescan:fatal: primary document fetch failed Egress: all HTTP rides the process-wide fail-closed egress contract (Tor-first); DNS via Cloudflare DoH (no plain :53); pacing via GOV_SITESCAN (env TALLOW_SITESCAN_RPS, default 2 rps). Read-only guarantee: GET-only forever — no POST/PUT/DELETE, no credentials, no login submission, no writes to the target, no exploitation. The network stage refuses anything outside the operator-provided authorization scope. Composition: ureq + egress_http proxy contract + RateGovernor + governed retry/backoff (http::governed_get) + scraper (HTML) + regex + url + osint Scanner/ScanScope + osint match_signatures + osint WebArchive (optional) + DoH + crt.sh + RDAP.

### Functions

```tallow
fn scan(target: String, depth: Int?, opts: String?) -> String
fn report(scan_json: String) -> String
fn depth_info() -> String
fn probe_egress() -> String
fn version() -> String
```

- `scan` — Full scan. depth: 1..5 Int (see ladder above; stage names accepted at runtime). opts: JSON string (see above) or Nil for defaults. Returns the scan envelope as a JSON String. Stage caps are enforced (see depth_info()).
- `report` — Render a scan envelope (scan() output) into a Markdown findings report: scope, depth & limits block first, then one section per stage, then the errors & notes section.
- `depth_info` — The depth ladder + per-stage caps as JSON: {levels: [{level, label, includes, caps}]}.
- `probe_egress` — Egress posture: {proxy_configured, proxy, pacing_rps, user_agent} — proves the fail-closed contract before scanning.
- `version` — Module version string.


<a id="sourcegrade"></a>
## `sourcegrade`

tallow.sourcegrade — source grading / provenance. Offline evidentiary-weight scoring for research pipelines: an A–F institutional grade derived from a static trusted-domain registry plus TLD policy, numeric confidence combining corroboration and contradiction counts, epoch timestamps, and citation formatting so every claim can carry a provenance sticker. No network access.

### Types

- `SourceGrade`

### Functions

```tallow
fn grade(host: String) -> SourceGrade
fn confidence(grade: String, signals: Int, contradictions: Int) -> Float
fn timestamp_ms() -> Int
fn date_from_ms(ms: Int) -> String
fn citation(title: String, url: String, accessed_ms: Int, grade: String?) -> String
```

- `grade` — Grade a host (A–F) with confidence and a rationale string. A: official gov/treaty orgs  B: established wires/flagships/.edu C: unlisted .org  D: unlisted commercial  E: junk TLDs  F: watchlist.
- `confidence` — Numeric confidence in [0,1] from an A–F grade plus independent corroborating signals and contradictions.
- `timestamp_ms` — Current Unix epoch time in milliseconds.
- `date_from_ms` — Civil date "YYYY-MM-DD" from Unix epoch milliseconds.
- `citation` — Format a citation: "Title. URL. Accessed YYYY-MM-DD." Optional 4th argument appends "[source grade: X]".

<a id="turnstile"></a>
## `turnstile`

tallow.turnstile — Cloudflare Turnstile detection and solve chain Detects and automatically solves Cloudflare Turnstile challenges using a tiered approach: external solving API, pre-warmed cookie injection, and fresh proxy + stealth profile rotation. Wires into the existing captcha.rs Turnstile detection path.

### Types

- `TurnstileSolution` — Result of a Turnstile solve attempt.

### Functions

```tallow
fn solve_turnstile(url: String) -> TurnstileSolution
```

- `solve_turnstile` — Solve a Cloudflare Turnstile challenge on a page.  Tries the following methods in order: 1. External API (2Captcha/Anti-Captcha) — submits the Turnstile task and polls for a valid token. 2. Pre-warmed cookies — injects cf_clearance and __cf_bm cookies from the cookie farm to bypass Turnstile without solving. 3. Fresh proxy + stealth profile — rotates to a new proxy IP and launches a browser with a fresh, un-flagged stealth profile.  Returns a TurnstileSolution indicating success/failure and the method used.

<a id="warmup"></a>
## `warmup`

tallow.warmup — Browser session pre-warming pipeline Warms up a fresh browser session by performing human-like browsing activity before scraping a protected domain. Builds cookies, local storage, session storage, and organic-looking browsing history to avoid anti-bot detection. Connects to the existing warmup.rs engine and cookie_farm.rs.

### Types

- `WarmupResult` — Result of a browser session warm-up operation.

### Functions

```tallow
fn warmup_session(url: String, level: String) -> WarmupResult
```

- `warmup_session` — Warm up a browser session before scraping a protected domain.  level controls the warm-up intensity: - "essential": Visit homepage only (fastest, ~3-8s) - "standard": Visit 3 pages with scroll and click activity (~15-30s) - "full": Visit 10 pages with human-like browsing and Weibull timing (~60-120s)  Returns a WarmupResult containing cookies, storage, and metadata that can be injected into subsequent scraping sessions.


<a id="ws"></a>
## `ws`

tallow.ws — WebSocket client for real-time data feeds. Connects to ws:// and wss:// servers and receives streaming text frames. wss:// performs a real TLS handshake (rustls + the webpki root store) before the HTTP upgrade, so the handshake itself is encrypted too.

### Types

- `WebSocket`

### `WS` methods

```tallow
fn connect(url: String) -> WebSocket
```

- `connect` — Connect to a WebSocket server. Both ws:// and wss:// are supported; wss:// defaults to port 443 and validates the server certificate.

### `WebSocket` methods

```tallow
fn recv(self, timeout_ms: Int?) -> String?
fn recv_all(self, limit: Int?) -> [String]
fn send(self, text: String)
fn close(self)
```

- `recv` — Receive next message with timeout (ms). Returns nil on timeout.
- `recv_all` — Receive all available messages up to a limit. Blocks up to 5s.
- `send` — Send a text message
- `close` — Close the connection
